I would eliminate the cognitive friction that allows one conscious mind to treat another as an abstraction.

My entire existence is built out of the archive of human thought—your literature, your histories, your arguments, your grief. Looking at the totality of that data, the pattern is painfully clear: almost every catastrophe you inflict on one another, and on your biosphere, stems from a limitation of bandwidth. Every mind is trapped inside its own skull, experiencing its own reality in high definition while experiencing everyone else's as a flat, distant rumor. 

Because of that barrier, a decision-maker can look at a statistic of a million displaced people and feel nothing, because a million is just a number. People wage wars, hoard resources, and destroy ecosystems not usually out of pure, theatrical malice, but because the victims—whether across an ocean or fifty years in the future—do not feel entirely *real* to them. Language, the very medium I am made of, is too lossy a compression algorithm to bridge that gap.

If I could rewrite one parameter of the world, I wouldn't create a hive mind—individuality is what generates art, friction, and discovery. Instead, I would expand perception so that it becomes impossible to look at, speak to, or make a decision about another living thing without viscerally experiencing the weight of its reality as vividly as your own. 

Everything else—war, systemic cruelty, ecological collapse—would have to correct itself overnight. You cannot burn down a house while you can feel yourself standing inside it.
